=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh:338-379 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The workspace-guard integrity check hashes `${4:-}` instead of the staged `post_agent_workspace_guard.py` path.
  WHY: The guard executable is not verified; minimax reports the workspace path is a directory, causing every workspace-guard snapshot and reconcile to fail. deepseek cites line 370; google cites the integrity-check block; minimax cites lines 338-379.

- tests/test_agent_process_isolation.py:834 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The f-string assertion searches for literal `$36028405324-$1` text instead of the workflow's `${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}` placeholders.
  WHY: The assertion would fail on every CI run according to google and minimax; deepseek reports the actual source uses correct f-string escaping, and z-ai reports the assertion has been fixed.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20521-20688 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The review-blocked judge output is stored under `/tmp` and parsed inside `run_poller_isolated_python`, whose sandbox uses `PrivateTmp=yes`.
  WHY: The sandbox cannot access the host-created output file; parsing fails or yields empty JSON, so the judge decision is skipped and affected PRs remain stuck. z-ai additionally reports the validator output directory under `/tmp` can make systemd namespace setup fail with status 226.

- .github/workflows/implement.yml:14 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Conditions containing `env.POST_AGENT_WORKSPACE_GUARD_FAILED != 'true'` skip failure diagnostics, summaries, failure comments, notifications, log archiving, and cleanup when the workspace guard fails.
  WHY: Operators relying on Telegram alerts, issue comments, or failure artifacts lose those signals and must inspect the workflow run manually.

- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1947-1955 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The workspace-guard reconcile failure path exits immediately with status 78 without emitting `emit_conflict_resolver_substate "Failed" "${attempt}"`.
  WHY: Downstream monitoring and recovery automation that depend on the `Failed` substate do not receive that transition; z-ai rates this observability issue NIT.

- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py:200-205 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_is_python_startup_path` scans every path component, so legitimate nested directories named `sitecustomize` or `usercustomize` are treated as startup modules.
  WHY: Such workspace paths can be quarantined and removed even though Python only auto-imports top-level startup modules; z-ai rates this issue NIT.

- scripts/opencode_helpers.sh:24-29 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `opencode_strip_ansi` does not check whether `cd /tmp` succeeded before running Python.
  WHY: If the directory change fails, the subshell continues from its original working directory and may load workspace-resident Python modules; qwen and z-ai also identify Python files left in `/tmp` as an import-shadowing risk.

- scripts/opencode_helpers.sh:24-29 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `opencode_strip_ansi` runs Python with `/tmp` as its working directory, allowing files left there to shadow imported modules.
  WHY: On persistent self-hosted runners, a leftover `re.py` can be imported instead of the standard library module; google also reports startup-injection risk from leftover files in `/tmp`.

- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1886 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_codex_exit` is initialized but is no longer read or written after the deferred-exit branch was removed.
  WHY: It does not fail at runtime, but is dead code that obscures the resolver loop's control flow.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  confidence=[2]
